title: Article 21 — Protection of life and personal liberty
summary: Article 21 states that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Its interpretation has developed through constitutional case law. The precise application depends on the facts and relevant judgments.

title: Article 14 — Equality before law
summary: Article 14 provides equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. How it applies in a specific dispute depends on the facts and applicable constitutional interpretation.

title: Consumer protection — general starting point
summary: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 provides a statutory framework for consumer rights and mechanisms for addressing qualifying consumer disputes. The appropriate forum, limitation period, evidence, and remedy depend on the transaction and facts. Check the Act and official consumer resources before acting.

title: Tenant rights — jurisdiction-specific information needed
act: Applicable state tenancy and rent laws
summary: Tenant and landlord rights can depend on the state or union territory, the applicable rent-control or tenancy law, the lease, and the circumstances. Before relying on a general answer, identify the property location and check the relevant state legislation. Do not assume one rule applies throughout India.

title: Employment rights — identify the applicable labour law
provision: Depends on employment type, location, and applicable law
summary: Employment entitlements can depend on the nature of employment, establishment, state, contract, and the law in force. For issues such as wages, termination, leave, or workplace safety, identify the relevant facts and verify the applicable central and state legislation or seek qualified advice.

title: Current criminal-law framework — Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
provision: Check the applicable provision and commencement
summary: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is part of India's newer criminal-law framework and replaced the Indian Penal Code for matters governed by the new law from its commencement, subject to applicable transitional rules. A question phrased using an IPC section may need to be mapped carefully to the relevant law and date; do not assume section numbers are interchangeable.

title: Legal aid — official starting point
provision: Eligibility and procedure should be checked with the relevant authority
summary: Free legal services may be available to eligible people through the legal services authorities system. Eligibility and the process depend on the governing rules and circumstances. Contact the relevant State Legal Services Authority or District Legal Services Authority to confirm options.

title: Theft — Section 303
summary: Section 303 defines theft and provides its punishment. The general punishment may extend to three years of imprisonment, or a fine, or both. For a second or subsequent conviction under this section, the provision prescribes rigorous imprisonment of at least one year and up to five years, along with a fine. A special proviso addresses a first conviction involving stolen property worth less than ₹5,000 where the property is returned or its value is restored; community service is prescribed in those circumstances. The applicable outcome depends on the statutory conditions and facts.

title: Snatching — Section 304
summary: Section 304 defines snatching as a form of theft involving the sudden, quick, or forcible seizure or taking away of movable property from a person or their possession. The prescribed punishment may extend to three years of imprisonment, and the offender is also liable to a fine. Whether the facts satisfy this provision depends on the circumstances.

title: Theft in specified locations or of specified property — Section 305
summary: Section 305 addresses specified forms of theft, including theft in a building, tent, or vessel used as a human dwelling or for custody of property; theft involving certain means of transport; theft of an idol or icon in a place of worship; and theft of government or local-authority property. The prescribed punishment may extend to seven years of imprisonment, and the offender is also liable to a fine. The specific statutory conditions must be checked against the facts.
